question: Which practical challenges do practitioners report at each stage of deploying machine learning in production?
contributions: Show that practitioners face challenges at each stage of the ML deployment workflow
Map reported case-study challenges to workflow steps (Table 1)
Discuss cross-cutting aspects: ethics, law, end users' trust, security
Outline potential solutions (tools and holistic approaches) and a research agenda

results.claim: Practitioners report problems at every stage of the ML deployment workflow (data management, model learning, verification, deployment) plus cross-cutting ethics, law, trust and security.
results.setup: Literature survey of case studies, review papers and lessons-learned papers from the last five years, organised by the Ashmore et al. four-stage workflow
results.quote: The main contribution of our paper is to show that practitioners face challenges at each stage

results.claim: Booking.com found that better model accuracy did not translate into business value after 150 deployed models, because proxy metrics such as clicks failed to track conversion.
results.setup: Booking.com, models deployed in production; reported in Sec 5.1
results.quote: Booking.com discovered after deploying 150 models into production

results.claim: Airbnb search started with a complex deep model, failed several deployments, and shipped a single hidden-layer network with 32 ReLU units to build the whole deployment pipeline.
results.metric: hidden units in first deployed model
results.setup: AirBnB search ranking; second hidden layer added later
results.quote: a single hidden layer NN with 32 fully connected ReLU activations.

results.claim: Training BERT-class NLP models can cost between $50k and $1.6m in cloud compute depending on model size.
results.setup: Full training of BERT, cloud computing prices, depends on model size

results.claim: One neural architecture search training cycle emits CO2 comparable to four average cars over their lifetimes.
results.setup: Estimate for one full training cycle with neural architecture search
results.quote: comparable to what four average cars emit in their whole lifetime

results.claim: Membership inference attacks reached 70% to 94% accuracy against models trained on ML-as-a-service providers.
results.setup: Attack against models trained on leading ML-as-a-service providers
results.quote: achieving anywhere from 70% up to 94% accuracy of membership inference.

limits: No interviews conducted; only published reports from the last five years (a few exceptions).
Paper selection procedure and number of papers reviewed are not stated.
Challenges are not prioritised or ranked; order in Table 1 does not reflect severity.
Requirements formulation stage and storage infrastructure are out of scope.
Authors concede the set of challenges is far from complete and that non-technical challenges are missing.
Tools in Sec 8.1 are illustrative, not a comprehensive review; the tool landscape has since moved on.
Notes a shortage of published deployment experience reports; industry knowledge goes unpublished.
practices: Start with a simple model to prove the concept and get the end-to-end pipeline deployed (Sec 4.1, Airbnb example).
Define domain and business-driven metrics alongside accuracy, and reuse them for production monitoring and model-update quality control (Sec 5.1).
Include data validation routines in the ML pipeline to catch data errors early (Sec 5.3).
Do not treat simulation-based testing as a full replacement for real-world testing (Sec 5.3).
Include researchers in the product codebase: same version control and code reviews (Sec 6.1).
Monitor input data, prediction bias, outliers and performance; expect to build custom checks because end-to-end platforms often do not fit (Sec 6.2).
Plan for concept drift detection and for continuous delivery across code, model and data (Sec 6.3).
Check that model updates are backward compatible with user trust (Sec 6.3).
Involve end users early and invest in tailored UI/UX (Sec 7.3).
Document datasets and models with datasheets, model cards and DVC-style version control (Sec 8.2).
Weigh risks and benefits before adopting holistic approaches such as DOA or MLTRL, as they need significant time investment (Sec 8.2).
